Wellcome Foundation ----- Appellant
Vs

full_judgment:
This appeal at the instant of the plaintiff is against the judgment and decree dated 10-7-2004 passed by the Court of 7th Additional District Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 29 of 2002 rejecting the plaintiff's application for temporary injunction. 

 2. The appellant as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 2 of 2002 for declaration of title and proprietary rights relating to the Trade Mark and for consequential relief. 

 The case of the plaintiff is that the plaintiff is a foreign company incorporated in the United Kingdom represented in Bangladesh, through their authorized representative and the plaintiff is a research based producer and merchants of Pharmaceutical, Veterinary and Sanitary substances and have been carrying on their business since long in the United Kingdom and also in all the countries of the world including Bangladesh and one of the Popular Trade Marks registered in Bangladesh in respect of Pharmaceutical, Medical and Veterinary preparations and substances falling under Class-5 containing the word mark 'SEPTRIM' is used in relation to Trimethoprim Sulphamethoxazide antibacterial agent and that the said trade mark is used by the plaintiff on strips, containers, packets, cartons etc. and the plaintiff's Trade Mark 'SEPTRIM' has a distinctive colour scheme, design, device and get-up and the said trade mark "SEPTRIM" has been registered in favour of The Well come Foundation Limited, trading as Burroughs Well come and Company, 183 Euston Road, London NWI 2 BP. England now at Berkeley Avenue, Greenford, Middlesex, UB6 ONW, United Kingdom being registration No. 769 in Class-5 in the office of Trade Marks Registry, Dhaka dated 4-1-73 and the registration of the above Trade Mark has been renewed by the authority concerned from time to time and the registration is still valid. The further case of the plaintiff is that the defendant started using a deceptively similar Trade Mark "SUPTRIM" together with the device, colour scheme, design and get-up in the similar type of products in inferior quality of goods with a view of marketing their inferior products and is creating contusion and deception in the markets amongst the innocent I unwary medical persons and public who while purchasing the inferior quality of medicine of the defendant are misled into thinking that they are in fact purchasing the genuine product of the plaintiff and the defendant is marketing their products in the market and thereby causing wrongful loss to the plaintiff. Further case of the plaintiff is that the trade mark, design, get-up, colour scheme of the defendants under the word mark "SUPTRIM" in respect of pharmaceutical and medical preparations and substances is visually and phonetically similar to the trade mark "SEPTRIM" in respect of pharmaceutical and medical preparations of the plaintiff and the defendants have adopted the device including the' design, get-up colour scheme of the plaintiff's superior product in the same design get-up, colour scheme as adopted by the plaintiff which is objectionable under section 10(1) and 8(a) of the Trade Marks Act, 1940. 

 3. After filing the suit, the plaintiff filed an application under Order XXXIX Rule 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restraining the defendant from manufacturing, marketing, using and selling the pharmaceutical, medical and veterinary preparations and substances and all other products under the Trade Mark "Suptrim". 

 4. The trial Court on 17-9-2002 issued a notice upon the defendant and the defendant opposite party thereafter filed written objection against the plaintiff's application for temporary injunction and the Court below by the order dated 10-7-2004 rejected the plaintiff's application for temporary injunction on hearing the parties. 

 5. Being aggrieved thereby, the plaintiff preferred the present appeal which was admitted by this Court and subsequently the plaintiff filed an application with a prayer for restraining the defendant opposite party, who are the respondent in the present appeal, from manufacturing marketing, using and selling the pharmaceutical, medical and veterinary preparations and substances and all other products under the Trade Mark "Suptrim" by an order of injection and accordingly a Rule was issued upon the defendant respondent opposite party and an adinterim order of restrainment was passed by this Court for a limited period. 

 6. Mr Mohammad Ohiullah, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant after placing the impugned order submitted that the Court below erred in law by not allowing the application filed by the plaintiff under Order XXXIX Rule 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure although the plaintiff was able to prove the prima-facie case for granting temporary injunction. He next submits that for the interest of justice the defendant should be restrained by an order of temporary injunction from adopting manufacturing, marketing, using and selling the pharmaceutical, medical and veterinary preparations and substances and all other products under the Trade Mark :Suptrim" together with the confusing similar monogram that is the plaintiff's monogram as adopted in their trade mark "Septrim". He next submits that the Court below did not take into consideration that the trade mark "Septrim" has been registered in the office of the Trade Mark Registry. Dhaka dated 4-1-73 by registration No. 769 in Class-5 and the registration for "Suptrim" has only been applied for before the Registrar of Trade Mark. The learned Advocate submits that the defendants are using a deceptively similar trade mark "Suptrim" together with the device, colour scheme design and get-up in the similar type of products in inferior quality of goods causing wrongful loss to the plaintiff and since the trade mark "Septrim" has already been registered in favour of the plaintiff, impugned order is liable to be set-aside. In support to his contention the learned Advocate has referred decisions as reported in 13 BLC (HC) 256, 50 DLR (HC) 348 and 54 DLR 394. 

 8. I have heard the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant and perused the documents placed before this Court. It appears that the plaintiff filed a suit for declaration of title and proprietary rights relating to the Trade Mark and for consequential relief and during the pendency of the suit, an application was filed for temporary injunction for restraining the defendant from manufacturing, marketing, using and selling the pharmaceutical, medical and veterinary preparations and substances and all other products under the Trade Mark "Suptrim". According to the plaintiff appellant, the product under the Trade Mark "Septrim" is manufactured by Glaxo Well come Bangladesh Limited and marketed by the plaintiff in its artistic design with specific colour, scheme. Plaintiff's trade mark "Septrim" has a distinctive colour scheme, design, device and getup which was registered in the office of trademarks registry, Dhaka on 4-1-73 and since then the plaintiff has acquired exclusive and monopoly right over the trade mark. "Septrim" but the defendants have started using a similar trade mark "Suptrim" together with the device, colour scheme, design and get-up in the similar type of products that is in relation to trimethoprim Sulphamet-hoxazole antibacterial agent in inferior quality and is creating confus on And deception causing wrongful loss to the plaintiff. 

 9. Section 8 of the Trade Mark Act 1940 imposes prohibition of registration of certain mattes and provides that no "Trade Mark nor part of a trade mark shall be registered which consists of or contains, any scandalous as designed, or any matter the use of which would by reason of its being likely to deceive or to cause confusion or otherwise, be disentitled to protection in a Court of justice. Section 10 of the Trade Mark Act 1940 enjoins prohibition of registration of identical or similar trade mark. On a visual comparison of the design and get-up of plaintiff's "Septrim" with defendants "Suptrim", much difference could not be detected and so it appears that there is a possibility of passing off. If there is a similarity between the two names which is likely to create confusion in the minds of the public that while they are doing business with the plaintiff, they are in fact doing the business with the other, then this comes within the ambit of passing off. Under such circumstances, the plaintiff is entitled to get an order of temporary injunction. The plaintiff being prima-facie owner and earlier user of the trade mark is entitled to an order of temporary injunction restraining the defendant. Plaintiff has a prima facie case and the balance of convenience and inconvenience is in favour of the plaintiff appellant the appellant will suffer irreparable loss and injury if temporary injunction is not granted in his favour till disposal of the suit. 

 10. This appeal has got merit for which it succeeds and thus is allowed. Order dated 10-7-2004 passed by the Court of 7th Additional District Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 29 of 2002 is set-aside. Plaintiff's petition for temporary injunction under order XXXIX Rule 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is allowed. Defendant respondent is restrained by an order of temporary injunction from directly or indirectly manufacturing, marketing using and selling the pharmaceutical medical and veterinary preparations and substances and all other products under the Trade Mark "Suptrim" till disposal of the suit. 

 11. Connected Civil Rule No. 516 (FM) of 2004 also stands disposed of in favor of the plaintiff appellant.
